description:
[PERF] compiler2 eagerly processes the entire runtime library on every compile, regardless of what the program uses.

Observed: `dbg(Enum.with_index(["a","b"], fn (x,_index) -> x <> "!" end))` takes ~1.34s end-to-end (debug build, fz2 interp). Not a churn/timeout (semantic analysis is bounded: 151 activation_analysis events). The cost is eager prelude intake.

Telemetry breakdown (/tmp/fz2-ewi.jsonl, 4293 lines):
  1474  fz.compiler2.job                     -- jobs driven for a one-liner
   737  fz.compiler2.work_graph.applied
   501  fz.compiler2.function.source.noted   -- ~500 library functions parsed+registered
   501  fz.compiler2.compiler_service.define
   454  fz.compiler2.macro.expanded          -- 454 macro expansions
   151  fz.compiler2.{activation_analysis,return_type}.defined
    26  fz.compiler2.function.defined         -- only ~26 functions actually compiled
    31  fz.compiler2.lowered_body.defined

Diagnosis: the whole runtime library (Enum, List, Enumerable, String, ...) -- ~500 functions and ~454 macro expansions -- is noted/macro-expanded/registered up front, but only ~26 functions are reached and compiled. ~500 functions of parse+expand overhead to run a program that touches three. The 1474 jobs and macro storm are downstream of this eager intake.

Fix direction: lazy / on-demand library intake -- note, macro-expand, and define a library function only when it is actually demanded (a function-source fact gated by demand), instead of eagerly processing the full prelude. Architectural; aligns with the incremental-fact-compiler direction (fz-rh2) and the strangler proposal.

Not blocking the fz-hwn.27 arc. Measure before/after with the same repro + telemetry event counts; target: function.source.noted and macro.expanded drop to ~the reachable set.
title: [PERF] compiler2 eagerly processes the whole runtime library on every compile
